children: Sandoz Group said it received approval from Canada's drug regulator for its generic version of Novo Nordisk's blockbuster diabetes drug Ozempic, advancing its efforts to build a portfolio of so-called GLP-1 medicines.

The Swiss maker of generic drugs said Friday that Health Canada granted it authorization to sell a generic version of semaglutide--the key ingredient in Ozempic and Novo Nordisk's sister weight-loss medicine Wegovy--for the treatment of adult patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
The company already received approval for a GLP-1 product in Brazil earlier this year, a semaglutide generic called Owozy that Sandoz will commercialize in the country in partnership with Adalvo.

Sandoz said nearly six million Canadians live with diabetes, with type 2 accounting for the vast majority of the patient population, and that the GLP-1 market in Canada is estimated to be valued at $2.6 billion.

The company doesn't anticipate any material earnings contribution this year from any potential launches of generic versions of semaglutide and the approval in Canada has no effect on its 2026 guidance, it said.
Sandoz separately said Friday it entered into a licensing, development, manufacturing and commercialization agreement with mAbxience for a generic version of Roche Holding's hemophilia drug Hemlibra.
